cluster_name: Meta settles US child safety lawsuit for up to $18 billion
tldr: Mother Jones is the single outlet whose headline abandons the settlement entirely, advertising a corporate-strategy frame ('Meta Doesn't Want to Be a Social Media Company Anymore') rather than any legal or safety angle — the maximum departure visible at the title layer. Twelve of the remaining twenty-three headlines lead with 'settles,' 'lawsuit,' or explicit dollar figures ($17–18B), collapsing the story into a legal-financial transaction. The body text's most prominent critical register — that the payment equals under 1% of annual revenue and Meta admitted no wrongdoing — is absent from every headline in the corpus, meaning readers who skim titles receive no accountability framing at all. El Pais is the only outlet to use the 'tobacco moment' analogy in its headline, the most historically ambitious framing in the corpus; no US outlet matched this register. Nordic and Politico Europe headlines foreground the EU's 'protect our kids' demand and 'Europe wants in' language, a regulatory-spillover angle that surfaces more prominently in their titles than in most body-text summaries.
event_summary: Meta settled a multi-state U.S. lawsuit for up to $18 billion, brought by 52 attorneys general alleging Facebook and Instagram were designed to addict and harm minors, agreeing to implement time limits and enhanced age controls while admitting no wrongdoing.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet whose headline drops the settlement entirely — 'Meta Doesn't Want to Be a Social Media Company Anymore' advertises a corporate-identity pivot, making it the maximum divergence from the legal-transaction consensus dominating every other front page.
Only outlet to use the 'tobacco moment' analogy in the headline itself, the most historically ambitious framing in the corpus; no US outlet matched this register at the title layer.

Only headline to embed a direct public dissatisfaction quote ('Not far enough') from parents and teens, making the PUBLIC_OPINION undercurrent surface-visible before the reader clicks — a rhetorical move absent from all other titles.

Frames the story as a systemic regulatory failure ('Why social media addiction is so hard to regulate') rather than a legal outcome — the only outlet whose headline foregrounds difficulty and structural limits rather than the settlement event.

Localizes the story entirely through a bilateral cybersecurity frame ('Roblox, Meta to beef up protection vs online threats'), removing the US lawsuit context and anchoring coverage in Philippine government meetings rather than the settlement.

bottom_line: Across 24 headlines the dominant signal is a legal transaction — 'Meta settles,' 'pays $18B,' 'landmark lawsuit' — while the body text's most damaging critical register (under 1% of annual revenue, no wrongdoing admitted) is invisible in every title; Mother Jones is the single outlet to break from the settlement frame entirely, and the EU regulatory-spillover angle is proportionally more prominent in Nordic and Brussels-focused headlines than in US and Canadian titles.
